items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: when I heard him play I realized he had something all of his own... I thought that Lester had the best taste of all of the tenor players.

ctx.x: I never heard anybody put it quite like that, and it held up. But, of course, I don't mean in any sense to compare myself to Hawkins. I think Hawkins when all the history is written and all put down, you would have to say that Hawkins was the father of the tenor saxophone-soloists. But, although I was a great -- although Lester Young started playing ten years, eight years after I played, when I heard him play I realized he had something all of his own that was -- I hate to use the word taste because taste means…
But to get back to Hawkins, he was a great musician, there's no doubt about that.
